comparator.name: Psychology
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated 2026–2027 guide controls this 180-EC pathway. The generic registry target includes English and Dutch teaching. Brain and Cognition is retained as the first detailed numbered public option and first dated study path, chosen independently of UCR fit. Its four named courses total 30 EC. The third year selects Behavioural Research Toolbox, the Brain and Cognition thesis, Consciousness: From Theory to the Clinic in period one, Psychology and AI in period two, and thirty genuinely open optional credits. Completing the full first year, research participation and common Year-2 courses meets specialisation entry; completing its full thirty credits including the toolbox meets the third-year methods threshold. The thesis follows the first part of the methods course. Zero-credit academic practicals, research participation and five colloquium points remain compulsory and are not added to the credit total.

components.name: Work and Organisational Psychology & Social Psychology
First-year Thesis
components.note: Academic-skills practicals and research participation are compulsory without additional credits. All earlier reading and writing assignments must be passed before the first-year thesis.

components.name: Scientific and Statistical Reasoning
components.note: This pathway completes all 60 first-year credits, including Research Methods & Statistics and research participation, before Year 2. The common courses require 48 or 60 first-year credits.

components.name: B&C Introduction to Neuroscience
components.note: One coherent Brain and Cognition specialisation is selected. Its four courses require the full first year and Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, completed before this semester.

components.name: B&C Toolbox: Experimental and Neuroscientific Methods
components.note: The 12-EC toolbox integrates behavioural experiments, neuroscience methods, data analysis, experimental design and Python programming.

components.name: Behavioural Research Toolbox
components.note: Entry requires the full first year, Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, Psychological Research and at least 18 EC of the specialisation, including its toolbox. All are completed in Year 2.

components.name: Bachelor's Thesis Brain & Cognition
components.note: The 12-EC empirical thesis follows the first part of Behavioural Research Toolbox. The earlier requirements and at least 18 specialisation credits must be passed. Five colloquium points must also be obtained; they add no separate degree credits. Students conduct supervised group research and write individual empirical reports.

components.name: Current Topics: Consciousness: From Theory to the Clinic
components.note: Selected from the restricted period-one Current Topics menu: consciousness research through psychological, neuroscientific and clinical approaches.

components.name: Current Topics: Psychology and AI
components.note: Selected from the restricted period-two Current Topics menu: the relationship between psychological science and AI. The full first year is required; prior AI or programming knowledge is not.

components.name: Optional course profile
components.note: Thirty EC remain genuinely open for a second specialisation, minor, exchange or an approved coherent course package. Individually chosen packages need Examination Board approval, research-university level, no overlap with Psychology and at most 12 first-year EC. No specific minor, course package or host is assumed.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest response combines substantial psychology, cognition and research with actual data and organisational methods. The clinical/health option and social/organisational option were then tested as coherent programme-interest priorities and each meets qualitative distinctness and the pairwise thirty-EC floor. Psychological Methods and Clinical Neuropsychology remain supported but unattempted after the maximum of three; neither is declared infeasible.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop empirical design, measurement, statistical testing and data analysis. UCR applies these across disciplines; UvA establishes the psychology-specific sequence.

Both involve psychological measurement, original data collection, quantitative analysis and empirical reporting. UCR studies leadership-related survey questions; UvA additionally constructs a psychological test and provides its prescribed test-theory sequence.

Both substantively examine statistical prediction and machine-learning approaches to data. UCR develops regression, classification and model evaluation in depth; UvA introduces behavioural big data, latent variables, network analysis and prediction from a psychology perspective.

Both examine the nature of mind, physical explanation and conceptual problems behind psychological science. UCR emphasises philosophy of mind; UvA also examines the history and general foundations of psychology.
Both examine neural anatomy, physiology and mechanisms underlying behaviour. UvA builds explicitly from molecular/cellular mechanisms to cortical and subcortical networks and research techniques.
Both examine sensory processing and the neural relationship between perception and action. UvA also addresses attention, multisensory integration and consciousness.

Both examine memory and emotion through cognitive neuroscience and neural dysfunction. UvA also gives substantial explicit coverage to language, while UCR includes attention, control and consciousness.
Both introduce brain organisation, mental processes and the relationship between neural function and behaviour. UvA also surveys the whole discipline of psychology.
Both substantively examine social cognition, attitudes, influence and group processes. The combined UvA component additionally covers work and organisational psychology.
Both develop empirical research design, statistical models and critical interpretation of psychological findings. UvA explicitly integrates scientific argumentation.
Both examine psychological disorder, symptoms, explanatory models and clinical perspectives. UvA additionally provides a distinct neurological-disorder and neuropsychology introduction.

Both develop psychological interviewing, reflection and interpersonal assessment skills. UCR embeds introductory practice in clinical assessment and therapy; UvA provides a dedicated general psychological-communication practical.
Both examine physical, cognitive, emotional and social development and biological/environmental influences across the lifespan.
No selected UCR course is a separately credited first-year psychology thesis.

Selected courses contribute experimental design, cognitive experiments and data methods elsewhere, but none reproduces this dedicated combination of neuroscientific measurement, behavioural paradigms and Python experiment/programming practice.

Advanced statistics, meta-analysis and computational study are represented elsewhere. None is counted again as this dedicated course in simulation studies, mathematical cognitive-task models and Python/PsychoPy experiment construction.
The 12-EC Brain and Cognition empirical thesis is compulsory at UvA. Optional UCR independent research is shown separately outside scheduled credits.
Higher cognitive study has its strongest placement with Memory, Language and Emotion. No additional course is counted as this dedicated experimental, neuroscientific and clinical consciousness topic.

The strongest selected statistical-learning relationship is placed with Behavioural Data Science. No additional course is counted as this integrated account of AI and psychology, their shared history and contemporary applications and ethics.
The thirty-credit optional profile is genuinely open; no particular minor, exchange host or course package is invented.

comparator.note: The 12-EC toolbox integrates behavioural experiments, neuroscience methods, data analysis, experimental design and Python programming.
Entry requires the full first year, Scientific and Statistical Reasoning, Psychological Research and at least 18 EC of the specialisation, including its toolbox. All are completed in Year 2.

The 12-EC empirical thesis follows the first part of Behavioural Research Toolbox. The earlier requirements and at least 18 specialisation credits must be passed. Five colloquium points must also be obtained; they add no separate degree credits. Students conduct supervised group research and write individual empirical reports.

notes.text: UCR can combine substantial psychological, cognitive, social, biological and data study. UvA provides a prescribed Psychology degree, specialist methods and practicals, and a compulsory Brain and Cognition thesis. The course relationships shown are partial; introductory clinical study at UCR does not confer professional qualification.

audience.programmeDescription: Psychology at UvA studies behaviour and mental processes through research, statistics and broad psychological foundations. This example follows the Brain and Cognition specialisation, with named current topics on consciousness and AI, an empirical thesis and thirty credits of open choice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines broad psychology with neuroscience, cognition and empirical data methods. Two further options emphasise clinical and health questions or social behaviour and organisations. UvA provides a more prescribed disciplinary and specialist practical sequence; the partial relationships do not reproduce its required thesis or confer clinical qualification.
